stem: A 13-year-old boy has polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, hyperglycemia, and circulating islet autoantibodies. Immune destruction of which pancreatic cell type is central to this disease?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Glucagon-producing alpha cells are being confused with insulin-producing beta cells.
options.explanation: Alpha cells produce glucagon; they are not the principal autoimmune target in type 1 diabetes.

options.label: B
options.misconception: A regulatory islet cell is being mistaken for the source of insulin.
options.explanation: Delta cells produce somatostatin, whereas beta cells provide insulin.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Exocrine pancreatic cells are being confused with endocrine islet cells.
options.explanation: Acinar cells make digestive enzymes and do not account for absolute insulin deficiency.

options.label: D
options.misconception: None; autoimmune beta-cell destruction produces absolute insulin deficiency.
options.explanation: Pancreatic beta cells synthesize insulin, and their immune-mediated loss causes type 1 diabetes.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Pancreatic duct physiology is being confused with islet endocrine function.
options.explanation: Ductal cells contribute bicarbonate-rich fluid, not insulin.

context: Learning objective: identify the cellular target in type 1 diabetes. Autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells causes progressive absolute insulin deficiency and hyperglycemia.
